summary: The ordinary single-result JSON routing and narration conversion are structurally consistent, and the focused verb tests pass, but the claimed flow/reaches --json refusal has a concrete argv hole. When --json occupies the required positional pattern slot, the depcruise branch parses only later tokens, treats --json as the pattern, runs dependency-cruiser, prints text to stdout, and exits 0.

findings.cause: The depcruise special case is entered whenever arg is present, before resolveInvocation validates flag-shaped positional arguments. It calls parseFlags(rest), so the second argv token is never inspected as a flag. The flags.json check at line 114 therefore misses --json when it is the arg itself.

expected.stderrContains: does not support --json or a positional-subject misuse diagnosis

actual.stderr: $ node tooling/src/ast/cli.ts flow --json\n[ast] verb=flow scope=corpus:depcruise(.dependency-cruiser.cjs)+--focus:--json langs=- scanned=n/a skipped=n/a(-) matches=0 status=complete\n

findings.testGap: tests/tooling/ast/cli.repo.int.test.ts:185 covers only flow packages/client --json, where --json is in rest. It does not cover the flag-shaped positional form that bypasses the new guard. This also leaves reaches --json exposed through the same branch.

findings.description: parseJsonSections discards every stdout line seen while no JSON object is open. The rot test therefore still passes if narration appears before, between, or after the five JSON values. It proves that five parseable objects occur in order, but not the claimed consecutive-values-only stdout protocol. Static inspection found rot narration routed through narrate and no current contaminating direct print in that verb, so this is a brittle proof rather than a second observed runtime failure.

stdoutWritersFound: tooling/src/ast/cli.ts imports print for usage output
tooling/src/ast/lib/emit.ts imports print for result/JSON output and human narration
tooling/src/ast/ops/depcruise.ts imports print for native text output
independentInventory.directChannelSearch: rg plus ast-grep found no console.log or process.stdout.write calls under tooling/src/ast; production print imports are limited to cli.ts, lib/emit.ts, and ops/depcruise.ts.

verification.result: FAIL against claimed contract: exit 0 with native text stdout

verification.command: ast-grep and rg direct-output inventory over tooling/src/ast/**/*.ts
verification.result: Three print-import owners; no console.log or process.stdout.write sites

observations: The 27-entry single-result-by-default denominator matches VERBS minus rot.
Every changed narration site reviewed now receives Flags and calls narrate; narrate preserves print on human runs and uses warn on JSON runs.
emit remains the JSON result writer and includes label, total, shown, hits, and additive meta.
rot retains five emit calls, and respell retains one exact emit plus one conditional near emit.
The ordinary tested depcruise form flow packages/client --json does refuse before beginRun, but that is only one argv ordering.
limitations: Per instruction, the already-completed approximately 220-second repository CLI suite was not rerun.
The existing /tmp/world-tools-json-output-report.json was read only as a lead; its all-verb run claims were not adopted as independent evidence.
No source or test files were edited. The focused test runner wrote only its normal ignored reports artifacts.
